policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the form simply as 'we' ('we will obey' and 'when we obey'), which is compatible with both first-person plural candidate forms and does not distinguish the qere from the ketiv; therefore the documented base fallback remains.

ASV 'ye have dealt deceitfully against your own souls' does not identify which candidate form it reflects. The note 'Or, in your souls' is classed alternative_rendering and therefore cannot decide the textual reading; both candidates remain compatible and the documented base fallback remains.
